overview.Module Title: Integrating STEAM in the 21st Century Classroom

sections.Aims and Fit of Module: This module explores innovative approaches to integrating Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) in the 21st-century classroom. Students will engage with inquiry-based, project-driven, and maker-centered pedagogies to design tangible and digital artifacts that bridge disciplines and connect to real-world contexts. To support students in developing 21st century competencies, this module emphasizes the following areas: • Provide students with hands-on learning experiences that integrate science, technology (including AI and AI-related tools and platforms), engineering, arts, and mathematics to foster interdisciplinary thinking. • Develop learner-centered environments that promote exploration, experimentation, and reflection through authentic STEAM challenges. • Leverage digital and physical tools (e.g., coding platforms, AI technologies, robotics, craft materials) to support prototyping and making in the classroom. • Help students develop confidence and competence to integrate STEAM principles into their teaching practices.
sections.Learning outcomes: A Critically analyse and synthesise the theoretical foundations and pedagogical principles of STEAM education, highlighting their significance in addressing 21st-century learning challenges. B Apply Research-Led Project-Based Learning (RLPBL) strategies to design and adapt student-centred STEAM activities for complex and authentic educational contexts that foster creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration. C Critically evaluate and integrate appropriate digital technologies (e.g., coding tools, AI applications, digital fabrication, VR/AR) and hands-on maker pedagogies to enhance STEAM curriculum design and instructional practice, with informed selection grounded in pedagogical justification. D Critically examine how digital data is produced, analysed, and interpreted in STEAM educational contexts, supporting evidence-based teaching decisions and curriculum evaluation.
sections.Method of teaching and learning: This module will consist of lectures and tutorials with implementing Research-Led Project-Based Learning (RLPBL) approach throughout this semester. Lectures will introduce core principles and foundations of STEAM education, familiarizing students with inquiry-based and project-based learning strategies, with AI-powered tools used to support dynamic content delivery and real-time engagement. Tutorials will leverage a variety of digital, physical and AI-enhanced tools, such as generative AI, to support students in tackling real-world problems through hands-on learning opportunities, meanwhile enhancing their critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration skills. Various instructional methods, including direct instruction, flipped classroom, hands-on learning, and fieldwork, with AI tools incorporated into each mode to offer personalized support for students. Both formative assessment and summative assessment will be applied, such as oral and written feedback from the instructor and peers. Students will be assessed at the midterm and at the end of the semester through an E-Portfolio. The E-Portfolio is a cumulative, critically reflective document that goes beyond artefact production. It requires students to engage with relevant literature, provide theoretical justification for design decisions, include reflexive commentary on their development as STEAM educators, and present evaluative analysis of their practice. The module employs a progressive model of collaboration. Students first engage with tasks individually to consolidate foundational understanding and develop the confidence and competence needed for meaningful contribution to group work. Group work is a deliberate pedagogical choice aligned with the collaborative and interdisciplinary nature of STEAM and Research-Led Project-Based Learning; it provides students with opportunities to develop team-working skills, negotiate roles, and engage in peer feedback processes that mirror authentic professional practice. To ensure accountability and equity, students are required to document their individual contributions and roles within the group clearly in the E-Portfolio. Peer assessment will be incorporated as a formative component, and mechanisms for managing group dynamics, including tutor mediation, will be scaffolded throughout the module.
